title: Jungle escape runner made with Claude Code: every animal needs a different move, and lions leap out of the bushes
author: vinishkapoor
selftext:
Roarway is a 3D lane runner in the browser, for desktop or mobile. You’re an explorer running across the jungle and savanna to reach a jeep waiting on the road, over 20 levels.

**Who made what:**

* **Code:** all written with Claude Code
* **Animal models:** from Sketchfab (CC BY 4.0), trimmed, resized and recoloured for the game
* **Sounds:** CC0 recordings from Freesound

**Workflow that worked:**

1. **Runner core first.** Three lanes, jump, slide and lane change, tuned on an empty trail until the moves felt responsive on both keyboard and swipe.
2. **One rule per obstacle.** Logs, rocks and roots get jumped, broken trees get slid under, and boulders need a lane change. Keeping each obstacle tied to one move made it readable.
3. **Animals follow the same idea.** Giraffes and elephants get slid under, zebras and warthogs get jumped, and charging rhinos need a lane change. The hardest part was the lions and cheetahs that burst out and leap at you, since you have to slide at the right moment. The timing and the warning before they jump took the most rounds with Claude.
4. **Fitting in outside models.** The Sketchfab animals came in at different sizes and styles, so they had to be resized and recoloured to match the bright look, then lined up with the hit areas the code uses.
5. **Difficulty curve last.** Each level is longer, faster and busier than the one before, with new animals brought in along the way. Stars reward escaping, collecting most of the golden fruit and a clean run with no stumbles.

[https://vinish.dev/roarway-jungle-escape-browser-based-game](https://vinish.dev/roarway-jungle-escape-browser-based-game)

Curious whether others mixing AI-written code with outside 3D assets hit the same scale and collision headaches.
